scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Blood looks the same in everyone, yet the wrong type in a transfusion can be dangerous. What makes blood types different?

scenes.name: antigens
scenes.text: Red blood cells carry markers on their surface, called antigens. The main ones are A and B.

scenes.name: types
scenes.text: Have A, you're type A. B, type B. Both, type AB. And neither, type O.

scenes.name: antibodies
scenes.text: Your plasma has antibodies against the antigens you don't have. Type A blood attacks B cells.

scenes.name: rh
scenes.text: Another marker, the Rh factor, decides positive or negative, like O positive.

scenes.name: donors
scenes.text: O negative red cells lack these main markers, so they're often used in emergencies, and called the universal donor.

scenes.name: match
scenes.text: Before a transfusion, labs test and crossmatch blood carefully. This is general info, not medical advice.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Antigens, antibodies, and Rh. Match before you transfuse. Follow for more on how things really work.
